Definition: to spy out, i.e. (generally) survey, (for evil) lurk for, (for good) care for
KeyPassages: Hosea 13:7; Job 20:9; Job 35:5; Song of Solomon 4:8
BiblicalUsage: Shur means to look, to spy out, to watch with care, and it is used for God and for men alike. The Lord says He will observe His people as a leopard by the way, Job is told to look to the heavens and see the clouds higher than he is, and the beloved is called to look from the top of Lebanon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God watches, and that is both comfort and warning. He observes the leopard's path and the heavens above me, and I hold that no watching of mine can match the watching of the Lord.
